chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That which Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) supplicated with against Dawud ibn Ali when he killed al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and seized the wealth of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was: 'O Allah! I ask You by Your Light which cannot be extinguished, and by Your Decrees which are not hidden, and by Your Might which does not expire, and by Your Favors which cannot be counted, and by Your Authority by which You restrained Pharaoh from Moses (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنَ خُنَيْسٍ: Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.بِعَزَائِمِكَ: By Your Decrees/Commandments, referring to firm divine determinations
key_terms.بِنُورِكَ: By Your Light, invoking divine illumination
key_terms.دَاوُدَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: Dawud ibn Ali, a prominent Umayyad governor and general
key_terms.فِرْعَوْنَ: Pharaoh, the archetypal tyrant in Islamic tradition
key_terms.مُوسَى: Moses, the prophet who confronted Pharaoh

ai.seo_question: What was the specific supplication Imam al-Sadiq made against Dawud ibn Ali?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) use of divine attributes during a period of political tension, specifically invoking Allah’s unquenchable Light and enduring Might to assert spiritual authority over the Umayyad governor Dawud ibn Ali. The reference to Pharaoh’s restraint by Moses serves as a potent metaphor for divine control over earthly powers, reinforcing the Shia theological concept of God’s absolute sovereignty amidst historical trials.
